chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from one of our companions, that he said:
There is no Zakat upon the gold dust (tibrs), but rather it is upon the Dinars and the Dirhams.
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat obligatory on raw gold dust or only on gold coins?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the Shia juristic view that Zakat on gold is tied to its status as currency (Dinars) rather than its mere existence as raw bullion or dust (Tibr). This distinction highlights the historical context where coined money served as the primary medium for wealth accumulation and trade, distinguishing it from raw precious metals which were often stored or used ornamentally without triggering the Zakat obligation until they reached the nisab threshold in a monetary form.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Jameel, from one of our companions that,
‘Heasws said: ‘There is no Zakāt upon the gold dust. But rather it (Zakāt) is upon the Dinars and the Dirhams’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “
Zakat is not due on gold. Zakat becomes due only on dinars and dirhams.”
